items.summary: Disposition: blocked for SearchWoot public beta or full launch; conditional for ordinary reversible growth that preserves existing consent, disclosures, provenance, claims, data-handling, and platform-policy boundaries. Keep the site private. Evidence: Woot documentation confirms API access but not redistribution, storage, derivatives, public display, caching, alerts, affiliate, advertising, image, price, trademark, attribution, freshness, correction, or takedown rights; current public terms restrict the proposed commercial/public uses. Human counsel is required before any rights-dependent launch, monetization, or permission outreach. Fleet compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 16 fail, 6 unknown, with 16 sites showing banner/consent/GA4-related failures and 4 privacy/terms findings. Analytics quality is yellow because source permissions or collector errors exist; this does not by itself block ordinary growth. Revenue evidence is partial: 18 named tracking rows plus one aggregate row, with $4.92 aggregate commission not assignable to a site. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates, permit only bounded reversible work, and continue the existing launch-readiness evidence work without closing unsupported tasks.

Launch-readiness tracking remains active: 0 of 4 tasks closed and 4 remain open. Evidenced progress includes official Woot API, terms, and support records; repository/configuration artifacts; privacy and cookie-policy artifacts; and draft site terms. No task may close because rights, field-level provenance, retention, deletion, correction, access, notification, GA4 settings, vendor coverage, incident procedures, accuracy/freshness, and rollback evidence remain incomplete. Next evidence action: attach and review one consolidated read-only bundle containing the field-level rights matrix, deployed data-flow and retention table, log/vendor/incident inventory, consent and GA4 configuration evidence, accuracy/freshness controls, and rollback evidence. Keep outreach, monetization changes, deployment, tracking changes, and launch-state changes paused.

Data-use dispositions: Woot API deal and price-history data — blocked. Missing current written permission or API agreement; field-level provenance; permitted storage, caching, display, derivatives, alerts, attribution, freshness, correction, takedown, trademark, image, price, affiliate, and advertising terms. Smallest next action: complete the internal counsel packet and obtain human-counsel review before any owner-authorized permission request. User alert rules and sync results — evidence_needed. Missing data inventory, identifiers, retention, deletion/correction/access workflow, processor terms, notification consent, and unsubscribe behavior. Smallest next action: produce a read-only deployed/repository data-flow and retention table. GA4 analytics — evidence_needed. Missing deployed consent and withdrawal behavior, GA4 property/data-sharing settings, retention settings, and jurisdictional treatment. Smallest next action: capture consent and GA4 configuration evidence without enabling new tracking. Operational logs and Cloudflare hosting data — evidence_needed. Missing log-field inventory, retention/access controls, vendor terms or DPA coverage, incident response, and data-subject request procedures. Smallest next action: produce a read-only log/vendor/incident inventory. No item is clear or conditional for public launch on current evidence.

Compliance scan is a technical baseline, not certification. Retain site-specific failures and unknowns for remediation or evidence; do not treat incomplete telemetry as zero or as an automatic blocker for ordinary growth. Affiliate and advertising use must retain visible disclosure and verified provenance; no unsupported claims, rights, attribution, ROI, or revenue conclusions are approved. Amazon reports 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate commission for 2026-09-21, but the commission is unattributed. Continue only existing reversible work that adds no new data collection, credentials, permissions, dependencies, cross-site behavior, monetization scope, or public exposure.
